prompt: A robot moves only right or down on an m×n grid. How many unique paths lead from the top-left to the bottom-right?
why: paths[r][c] = paths[r−1][c] + paths[r][c−1]. Fill the table row by row.
trap: Backtracking lists every path; you only need to count them.

prompt: What is the minimum number of inserts, deletes and replacements to turn one word into another?
why: dist[i][j] over prefixes of both words: match for free, or take 1 + the best of insert, delete, replace.
trap: BFS over strings works in theory, but the state space explodes; two prefixes make a small table.

prompt: Given two strings, find the length of their longest common subsequence.
why: lcs[i][j] = lcs[i−1][j−1] + 1 on a match, else the max of dropping a letter from either string.
trap: Two pointers can check one subsequence, but finding the longest shared one needs every prefix pair.

prompt: Each cell of a grid has a cost. Moving only right or down, find the path from corner to corner with the smallest total cost.
why: best[r][c] = cost[r][c] + min(best above, best left). No cycles, so no Dijkstra needed.
trap: Greedily stepping to the cheaper neighbor can walk into an expensive region later.

prompt: In a 0/1 matrix, find the area of the largest square containing only 1s.
why: side[r][c] = 1 + min(above, left, diagonal) when the cell is 1.
trap: A monotonic stack solves the largest rectangle; a square has a simpler table.
